top_choice_rationale: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics is a single dated two-author 1985 step, independently reproduced and used for four decades, that made bond breaking, proton transfer and reactions in water and at surfaces computable without fitted force fields. Attribution is clean and the citation can be anchored to the 1985 unification. It is a method prize close to condensed-matter physics, but it is the best-defended claim on the slate. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles rank second for their mechanistic chemistry and medical reach despite the unsettled attribution; Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is mature but follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize; no award is last because mature, defensible work exists.
